Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From cb0b430b4e3acc88c85e0ad2e25f2a25a5765262 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Mar 2022 08:26:02 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] net: dsa: Add missing of_node_put() in dsa_port_parse_of

The device_node pointer is returned by of_parse_phandle()  with refcount
incremented. We should use of_node_put() on it when done.

Fixes: 6d4e5c570c2d ("net: dsa: get port type at parse time")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220316082602.10785-1-linmq006@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/dsa/dsa2.c b/net/dsa/dsa2.c
index 074e4a69a728..88e2808019b4 100644
--- a/net/dsa/dsa2.c
+++ b/net/dsa/dsa2.c
@@ -1436,6 +1436,7 @@ static int dsa_port_parse_of(struct dsa_port *dp, struct device_node *dn)
 		const char *user_protocol;
 
 		master = of_find_net_device_by_node(ethernet);
+		of_node_put(ethernet);
 		if (!master)
 			return -EPROBE_DEFER;
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/dsa/dsa2.c`**
   - A new line was added to call `of_node_put(ethernet);` after the `master` variable is assigned the result of `of_find_net_device_by_node(ethernet);`. This ensures that the reference count of the `ethernet` device node is decremented properly when it is no longer needed.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a resource management issue by ensuring that the reference count of the `ethernet` device node is properly managed. The original code did not release the reference obtained from `of_parse_phandle()`, which could lead to memory leaks. By adding the `of_node_put()` call, the patch fixes this oversight, thereby improving the stability and reliability of the code. This change is directly related to the previous commit identified by the Fixes tag, which introduced the parsing of the port type at parse time but did not handle the reference count correctly.
